stage1.impression: A tidy, competent CG interior of a narrow bar: a slatted timber wall with a glowing band of fins above, a long dark counter with stools, a bottle shelf and a banquette. At 1:1 it reads as a render. The band glows flat salmon-pink and clips, the slatted wall is the brightest surface in the room with a hot scallop at its top, the counter face looks like rubber granulate rather than terrazzo, the bar top is a featureless black slab, and the ceiling and right wall are empty dark planes. The frame has no visible speaker and no sign of people. A magazine would see a generic, slightly showroom bar, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The lantern's band reads amber, not salmon-pink (delta_e vs #FFB000 under 12 in [280,180,900,245]) and does not clip (clip_pct < 1)
The slatted baffle is no longer the brightest surface: lum_median of [280,255,615,610] at or below 85, with the light pooled on the counter and the porch instead
Clear pools of light on the bar top with dark between them, the quartzite reading as stone (visible veining and a soft sheen at 1:1)
The terrazzo counter face reads as honed terrazzo: finer chips, a lighter ground, a soft sheen, not rubber crumb
Some sign of life: a record out of its sleeve, a coat on a stool, half-drunk glasses, a stool turned off axis
An EARF product legible as the frame's one point of colour. A Core or Hemisphere in its tint should read; the pendants now read neutral grey-white
The ceiling and the right wall hold some detail (lum_median >= 22) instead of reading as empty planes
No 'generic bar' read: the lantern must read as a freestanding oak box with a porch, which means a visible shadow gap or foot line and a dark reveal around it

defects.what: The acrylic band glows flat salmon-pink (RGB 249/185/169) and clips 5.2 %. It reads as a lightbox or signage, not thick amber cast fins with glowing edges
A clipped hot scallop of a downlight on the baffle just under the band (clip 1.6 %, lum_median 232)
The slatted oak baffle is the brightest large surface (median 123), lit flat and evenly. It reads as a laminate slat wall and fights the counter for attention
The quartzite bar top reads as a flat black slab with no veining and no pools of light from the counter spots
The counter's terrazzo face has coarse, multicoloured chips on a dark ground. It reads as rubber crumb or cork
The pendant shades are neutral grey-white (R=G=B at about 177) in a warm 2800 K frame. They look cold, with no tint and no glow
The ceiling is an empty, near-black plane (median 13) with a stray diagonal light streak near x 420-500
The right wall is a dark featureless plane (median 19) with a hard diagonal light edge. The plaster has no texture at 1:1
The banquette leather reads as flat red-brown with no sheen, creasing or seams. The oak cap rail is lit flat
The back-bar bottles are repeated copies of the same few models at regular spacing
The porch's oak boards are identical in tone with no grain at 1:1. The box does not read as standing free: no foot line or shadow gap is visible
Seven identical stools in a perfect row with no variation. The room is empty of life

changes.problem: The band reads salmon-pink and clips, which makes it signage instead of lit amber acrylic.

change.setting: the lantern's band: emission (and its colour behind the Smoke fins)
change.from: 3.0, a near-white source that the warm grade tints pink
change.to: 1.6, with the source at about 2000 K / amber #FF9A30 so that the Smoke fins pass a deep amber; light the fin edges brighter than their faces

changes.expected: An amber band holding fin detail, with brighter fin edges and no clipping. It becomes the frame's warm accent instead of a pink lightbox.

changes.problem: The baffle is lit flat and is the brightest surface, with a clipped downlight scallop at its top.

evidence.measured: lum_median 122.6, p95 219, the scallop at [540,236,600,270] clips 1.6 %

change.to: 0.6 W/m2, 2400 K, moved tight to the baffle so that it rakes the slots from below and falls off upward. Re-aim or drop the downlight that scallops under the band

changes.expected: The slots read in relief with deep shadow lines. The baffle steps back to about median 75 and the eye goes to the counter and the porch.

changes.problem: The bar top has no pools of light and reads as a flat black slab.

evidence.measured: lum_median 62.7, p95 133, no visible pool pattern along the counter

change.to: 22.0 W, 14.0 deg, 2700 K, aimed so that each spot lands on the quartzite at a glass, with dark between the pools

changes.expected: Distinct oval pools on the stone that catch the glasses, with highlights on the stone's sheen and dark gaps between.

changes.problem: The quartzite and the terrazzo face don't read as real stone at 1:1.

evidence.measured: Seen at 3x: coarse multicoloured chips on a dark ground (median 23-63). The top is uniform black with no veining

change.setting: the terrazzo's chip size and ground tone; the quartzite's finish
change.from: coarse multicolour chips on a dark ground; a uniform black top
change.to: chips of 4-12 mm in two or three warm greys and ochres on a mid warm-grey ground, honed with roughness about 0.35. The quartzite gets low-contrast veining and a roughness of about 0.25

changes.expected: The counter reads as honed terrazzo with a soft sheen under the spots. The top reads as stone and holds the pools from c3.

changes.problem: The pendants read as cold, neutral grey shades in a warm room, so no EARF product carries colour.

change.setting: the Cores' and Hemispheres' own glow, and the white balance
change.to: light the tinted shades from inside at 2400 K so that their tint glows through. Keep white_balance_k at 2800

changes.expected: The lamps glow in their tint (r_median well above b_median) and become the EARF accent in this frame.

changes.problem: The room is empty and staged, with no sign of life.

evidence.measured: Seven identical stools in a perfect row, and only four placed glasses on the counter

change.to: add a record out of its sleeve with the sleeve leaning on the counter, two half-full glasses and a napkin at the near end, a coat over the third stool, two stools turned 10-20 deg, and a menu on a banquette table

changes.expected: The room reads as in use at night, without crowding the counter's pools.

changes.problem: The ceiling and the right wall are empty dark planes, and the right wall has a hard diagonal light edge.

change.setting: the fill, and the banquette: 4 x spot
change.from: fill area 0.02 W/m2, 2900 K; banquette spots 9.0 W, 16 deg
change.to: fill 0.05 W/m2, 2700 K; banquette spots 11.0 W, 24 deg, aimed to wash the plaster just above the cap rail. Remove the hard diagonal edge

changes.expected: The plaster shows its texture in a soft falloff above the banquette. The ceiling holds faint detail. The leather picks up a sheen.

changes.problem: The lantern doesn't read as a freestanding box: its foot line and the reveal around it are invisible.

evidence.measured: No distinct light line at the porch's foot. The base runs straight into the floor tone

change.to: 6.0, kept narrow, with a dark shadow gap above it

changes.expected: A thin warm line under the box and the porch shows that the lantern floats on its own floor, so the room reads as a specific place.

out_of_scope.request: Show the Tropos pair (Ember) in this frame as the one saturated hero
out_of_scope.why: The pair is inside the lantern as placed and this camera cannot see it. The products' placement is fixed. A frame that sees the speaker needs another camera through the porch, which is a different shot.

out_of_scope.request: Vary the back-bar bottles and the stool models
out_of_scope.why: These are asset changes beyond small props. The bottles repeat visibly, so a varied bottle set would help if it is allowed as props.
